label: canon-c19-in13-n2
_why: THE COST-SLOPE SWEEP, BATCH 3 - THE x1.3 LIFT AT THE FOUND SLOPE (the plan's last step: 'then the x1.3 lift at the found C'). Batch 2, canon-c19-in12 (session 20260914_173832), landed in the GDP band in its first run: 1.04 / 0.97 / 0.96 / 0.93 / 0.84 / 0.85 / 0.75 / 0.86 / 0.91 / 1.04 / 1.09x vanilla's median at 1840..1935 (1.11x at 1936) - a dip to 0.75x at 1900 while the frontier was dear, then realignment by the 1930s - with productive workers per capita 0.65x (in the target band), GDP per productive worker 1.61x, rung 0 at 45% staffed and a 22% margin against the frontier's 44-48% (the first book whose margins are NOT flat across the eras), tiered levels half of vanilla's count, peasants ABOVE vanilla's share in most majors, pools 0.64 of GDP. So C 1.9 is the slope, and this book raises rung 0's input value from x1.2 to x1.3 on it (canon-c19-in13 = canon-c19-in12 with --in0 1.3; the ladder anchored on the lifted rung 0, so every rung's input value rises by 1.3/1.2) - the user's original lean (canon-flat-in13, 2026-09-10), to push rung 0's break-even output price up and make it die rather than thin. Rung 0's textile target_be reads 103 (marginally loss-making at base), as flat-in13's did.
